scope: Batches 13–15, 28 meanings and 84 offline question bands

items.reviewNote: In chapter IV 109:83, pouce means thumb; opposable finger. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The body part is the opposable thumb, not a unit of length; all Level 4–5 alternatives are masculine singular digits.

In chapter IV 109:160, excès means excess; extreme degree. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 110:101, baleines means whales; large marine mammals. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. This plural refers to the same animal sense as singular baleine in the preceding passage; keep distinct surface questions.

In chapter IV 110:136, raisonneur means reasoner; one fond of reasoning. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 110:189, tirait means derived; drew from a source. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. D’où un atome tirait son mouvement asks about the source of motion, not physical pulling or shooting.

In chapter IV 110:200, mouvement means movement; motion. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 110:226, idées means ideas; thoughts. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 111:22, embarrassé means perplexed; at a loss. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The giant is perplexed by the question of an âme in the whale; the earlier embarrassa lemma is planned for a different reflexive action.

In chapter IV 111:38, examina means examined; inspected carefully. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 111:60, patiemment means patiently; without haste. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 111:154, logée means housed; lodged within. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The hypothetical soul would reside inside the animal; the wording is figurative and feminine singular.

items.meaning: were inclined; tended toward a belief
items.reviewNote: In chapter IV 112:19, inclinaient means were inclined; tended toward a belief. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The movement toward a belief is figurative, without certainty or a physical lean.

In chapter IV 112:38, penser means to think; to believe. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 112:186, flottait means was floating; remained on water. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 113:20, temps-là means that time; that period. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The attached -là points to a specific period mentioned by the narrator; preserve the historical form and demonstrative.

In chapter IV 113:59, revenait means was returning; came back. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 113:71, cercle means circle; line of latitude. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. Cercle polaire is the geographic latitude circle, rather than a social group or drawing tool.

In chapter IV 113:78, polaire means polar; near a pole. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 113:125, observations means observations; things noticed and recorded. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 113:163, avisé means thought of; conceived. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The negative personne ne s’était avisé means nobody had thought of the observations; distinguish the published aviser senses.

In chapter IV 114:4, gazettes means newspapers; gazettes. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The gazettes report an alleged shipwreck; these are news periodicals, not private letters.

In chapter IV 114:29, vaisseau means ship; sea vessel. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

items.meaning: ran aground; was wrecked on shore
items.reviewNote: In chapter IV 114:38, échoua means ran aground; was wrecked on shore. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The vessel reaches the coasts of Botnie and runs aground, a nautical use, rather than merely failing at a task.

In chapter IV 114:49, côtes means coasts; shores. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.

In chapter IV 114:76, eurent means had; experienced. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. Eurent de la peine means experienced difficulty; the past historic form shares the existing avoir possession/auxiliary sense.

In chapter IV 115:17, ingénument means candidly; without artifice. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The narrator claims candor and no embellishment, with ironic force in the final sentence.

In chapter IV 115:46, passa means happened; took place. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. Se passa describes what happened, matching the existing passer event sense, rather than movement past a place.

In chapter IV 115:123, historien means historian; writer of history. The questions contrast this contextual sense and preserve its source use. The source context and each three-band contrast were checked for the target meaning, agreement and one intended answer.
